speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms of dizziness and imbalance, can you tell me if the room feels like it is spinning around you (vertigo) or if you just feel lightheaded? Also, do you have any hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the dizziness get worse with specific head movements, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, have you noticed any pain behind your eyes or sensitivity to light?

text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the dizziness is constant and not clearly triggered by specific head movements, I need to check for signs of central nervous system involvement. Do you have any difficulty walking straight, slurred speech, or double vision? Also, have you had a fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, vomiting, significant headache, ear pain, recent foreign travel, known exposure to toxins or use of new medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, the absence of fever and severe headache helps rule out some infectious or vascular causes. I need to perform a physical exam to assess your vestibular function; please sit up and turn your head quickly to the right and left while keeping your eyes open (Head Impulse Test). Do you notice any jerk of your eyes trying to catch up, or do your eyes stay fixed on my nose?

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful information. Based on your recent cold and constant vertigo, I suspect Vestibular Neuritis, but I need to rule out Labyrinthitis. Can you confirm if you have any hearing loss or tinnitus in the affected ear?

REQUEST TEST: Audiogram
